pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Isolate a possibly infected device first
steps.body: Discord account theft often comes with a token stealer. Sign out on the infected device and do not reuse it until cleaned.

steps.title: Change your password from a clean device
steps.body: Changing your Discord password logs out all other sessions, revoking a stolen token.

steps.title: Enable two-factor authentication
steps.body: Turn on 2FA so a stolen password or token alone cannot take the account back over.

steps.title: Report the compromised account to Discord
steps.body: Use Discord's official support flow to report the compromise and recover access if you are locked out.

steps.title: Review authorized apps and bots
steps.body: Check which third-party apps and bots have access and revoke anything you do not recognize.

pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Act immediately on the change notice
steps.body: If you received an "email changed" notice you did not make, act now — an attacker is taking over the account.

steps.title: Use a clean device
steps.body: If malware is suspected, do not sign in from the possibly infected device until it is cleaned.

steps.title: Recover through official support
steps.body: Use Discord's official account-recovery process to prove you own the account — never a third-party service.

steps.title: Restore your email and enable 2FA
steps.body: After regaining access, restore your email address and turn on two-factor authentication.

pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Use your saved backup codes
steps.body: If you saved recovery codes when you set up two-factor authentication, use one now to sign in.

steps.title: Recover through official support
steps.body: If you have no backup codes, use Discord's official account-recovery process — never a paid third-party service.

steps.title: Re-enable two-factor authentication
steps.body: Once you are back in, set up two-factor authentication again so the account is protected.

steps.title: Store new backup codes offline
steps.body: Save the new recovery codes somewhere safe and offline.

steps.body: Check your Steam purchase history for charges you did not make, and do not click links in unexpected receipt emails.

steps.title: Secure the account first
steps.body: Change your password and enable two-factor authentication so a thief cannot keep spending.

steps.title: Report the unauthorized charge
steps.body: Dispute the charge through Steam's official support — never a third-party refund service.

steps.title: Review saved payment methods
steps.body: Remove or replace any card or payment method you do not recognize.

pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Use a clean device
steps.body: If malware is suspected, avoid signing in from the infected device until it is cleaned.

steps.title: Secure the Microsoft account email
steps.body: Confirm you still control the email address and enable its own two-factor authentication.

steps.title: Use Microsoft's official account-recovery form
steps.body: Submit Microsoft's account recovery form; do not trust third-party 'recovery agents'.

steps.title: Turn on two-step verification or passwordless sign-in
steps.body: Enable Microsoft two-step verification (or go passwordless) so a stolen password alone cannot re-take the account.

steps.title: Review devices and recent sign-ins
steps.body: Remove unfamiliar devices from your Microsoft account after regaining access.

pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Act immediately on the change notice
steps.body: If you received an "email changed" notice you did not make, act now — an attacker is taking over the account.

steps.title: Use a clean device
steps.body: If malware is suspected, do not sign in from the possibly infected device until it is cleaned.

steps.title: Recover through official support
steps.body: Use Xbox's official account-recovery process to prove you own the account — never a third-party service.

steps.title: Restore your email and enable 2FA
steps.body: After regaining access, restore your email address and turn on two-factor authentication.

pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Use your saved backup codes
steps.body: If you saved recovery codes when you set up two-factor authentication, use one now to sign in.

steps.title: Recover through official support
steps.body: If you have no backup codes, use Xbox's official account-recovery process — never a paid third-party service.

steps.title: Re-enable two-factor authentication
steps.body: Once you are back in, set up two-factor authentication again so the account is protected.

steps.title: Store new backup codes offline
steps.body: Save the new recovery codes somewhere safe and offline.

pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Recover the linked email account
steps.body: First recover access to the email address through its own provider — most account controls rely on it.

steps.title: Recover through official support
steps.body: If you cannot recover the email, use Xbox's official account-recovery process to prove ownership another way.

steps.title: Update the linked email
steps.body: Once back in, change the linked email to one you control.

steps.title: Enable two-factor authentication
steps.body: Turn on two-factor authentication so the account is not tied to a single email.

pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Stop communicating and do not pay
steps.body: Stop responding to the "recovery service" and do not send more money — a scammer who has already defrauded you is unlikely to return the account even if paid.

steps.title: Change passwords from a clean device
steps.body: Change your password and any passwords you reused, from a device you trust.

steps.title: Report the scam
steps.body: Report the scammer to Xbox and to your payment provider if you paid.

steps.title: Recover through the official process
steps.body: Recover the account through Xbox's official process — never a paid third party.

pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Stop using the possibly infected device
steps.body: Sign out and stop using the device until it has been scanned and cleaned. Use a different trusted device for the next steps.

steps.title: Scan the device
steps.body: Run a reputable antivirus or anti-malware scan and remove anything it flags before signing in again.

steps.title: Change passwords from a clean device
steps.body: After cleaning, change your password from a device you trust — not the infected one.

steps.title: Recover the account if it was taken
steps.body: If the account was already stolen, follow Xbox's official account-recovery process.

pages.disclaimer: The Grid Nexus does not recover accounts or request account credentials. Follow the official process.

steps.title: Change your password
steps.body: Change your password from a device you trust, in case someone else is already signed in.

steps.title: Sign out of other sessions
steps.body: Revoke unfamiliar sessions and devices through Xbox's account settings.

steps.title: Enable two-factor authentication
steps.body: Turn on two-factor authentication so a stolen password alone cannot take the account back.

steps.title: Review recent activity
steps.body: Check for changed email, phone number, linked accounts, or messages you did not write.
